issues.source_quote: Это не актуально!
issues.translation_quote: They're out of fashion!
issues.justification: 'Не актуально' means 'not relevant/topical' and is a dismissal of the idea; 'out of fashion' shifts the meaning, and the irony of the line is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Разрешите хотя бы… - Вот это попробуйте!
issues.translation_quote: At least let me... - Try that!
issues.justification: In the original the colonel hands over something (the pistol/instrument) or points to a concrete option; the translation is vague and the comic point of the exchange (colonel refusing every suggestion until one is allowed) is blurred.

issues.source_quote: Упал, выругался... Чёрт возьми! Ух, прости, "Чёрт побери!"
issues.translation_quote: "Damn!" Oh, sorry: "Damn it!"
issues.justification: The joke depends on two distinct but near-identical passwords (чёрт возьми vs чёрт побери); the English renders them nearly identically, so the point about not confusing the exact phrase is lost.

issues.source_quote: Щёрт побери, щёрт побери!
issues.translation_quote: Damn it! Damn it!
issues.justification: The foreign-accent mispronunciation (щёрт, шьёрт) that characterizes the fake foreigners' speech is flattened; the comic accent is lost entirely.

issues.source_quote: Х-х-х-х-ха... Нет, шуба подождёт. Я считаю, главное - это поглядеть мир!
issues.translation_quote: Ha-ha-ha... - No, the fur coat can wait.
issues.justification: The interviewer's lines and Gorbunkov's lines are not attributed; with the missing laugh and run-together dialog, the exchange is confusing. Also 'Угу... значит Вы ещё никогда…' rendered as 'I see... So you've never...' is OK, but the dialogue structure is garbled.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках! Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: Drop dead! May I see you in a coffin, wearing white slippers! May you have to live on your salary alone!
issues.justification: The Odessan/Yiddish-inflected non-standard speech of the curse (исдох, у гробу, у белых тапках) is rendered in neutral standard English, losing the colorful character voice.

issues.source_quote: Такси? Говорит Семён Семёнович Горбунков. ... Пришлите такси
issues.translation_quote: Taxi service? This is Semyon Semyonovich Gorbunkov.
issues.justification: Fine in itself, but the translation of 'Ага, следит, пусть видит, что я пью' is acceptable; the more significant issue is 'Ку-ку... За твою премию!' where 'Ку-ку' is rendered as 'Cuckoo', a drinking-toast gesture that is unclear in English.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a whole sheaf of tickets and win... a pumping station!
issues.justification: The rhyme (пачку/водокачку) and comic mock-slogan are lost; no rhyming equivalent is attempted.

issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron's hot— without leaving the cash register!
issues.justification: Acceptable literal rendering, but the character's catchphrase mixes two idioms for comic effect; the English 'cash register' loses the Soviet 'касса' pun slightly. More importantly, 'Пятый, пятый' etc. are fine. Minor humor loss.

issues.source_quote: Ваш муж заплатил 97 рублей 18 копеек
issues.translation_quote: According to the report, your husband paid 97 rubles and 18 kopecks for a single broken mirror!
issues.justification: Source says 'зеркальное стекло' (plate glass window), not a mirror; mistranslation changes the event.

issues.source_quote: Читали в «Неделе», отдел для, дома для семьи...
issues.translation_quote: Didn't you read it in Nedelya, the home and family section?
issues.justification: Cultural reference to the Soviet weekly 'Nedelya' is left untranslated and unexplained, so target viewers miss that this is a pseudo-authoritative magazine source.

issues.source_quote: Мя-аув!
issues.translation_quote: Meow!
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Лёлик только без рук' rendered 'keep your hands off me' is OK. Minor: 'Закрытый перелом' vs 'открытый перелом' rendered 'simple' vs 'compound' fracture, which loses the opposition closed/open that Nadya's joke relies on.

issues.source_quote: Врачи рекомендуют: успокаивает нервную систему
issues.translation_quote: Doctors recommend it: calms the nerves
issues.justification: Minor; the reference to the magazine and the pseudo-medical claim about the drink are acceptable but the unspecified 'it' loses the fact that the captain is pushing vodka.

issues.source_quote: Будет тебе там и ва-анна, будет и кофэ, будет и какава с чаем...
issues.translation_quote: You'll have your ba-ath there, and your coff-ay, and your choccy with tea...
issues.justification: The humor derives from the thugs' mocking repetition of a classic Soviet line; 'choccy' is a British colloquialism clashing with the rest of the text.

issues.source_quote: Пейте. Пейте, пейте...
issues.translation_quote: Drink. Go on, drink...
issues.justification: Acceptable; however 'Пошёл! Клиэнт прибыл!' rendered 'Go on! The mark has arrived!' is slightly off for a radio code.

issues.source_quote: Ну-с, начнём, пожалуй!
issues.translation_quote: Well then, let's begin!
issues.justification: The archaic/jocular suffix 'ну-с' is lost; minor register flattening.

issues.source_quote: Я встретил Вас и всё былое В отжившем сердце ожило...
issues.translation_quote: I met you, and all the past Stirred in my long-dead heart...
issues.justification: 'Отжившем' means worn-out/outlived, not 'long-dead'; slight overstatement.

issues.source_quote: Нет, на это я пойтить не могу!
issues.translation_quote: No, I can't go along with that!
issues.justification: The deliberately comic non-standard 'пойтить' (Gorbunkov's feigned naivety) is not reflected.

issues.source_quote: Строго на север, порядка... 50-ти метров, расположен туалэт, типа сортир
issues.translation_quote: Due north, approximately... fifty meters away, is the lavatory, as in the crapper
issues.justification: Diagram letters 'Мэ' and 'Жо' (М/Ж) are rendered 'M' and 'W', losing the joke on the crude pronounced forms.

issues.source_quote: Гэ-э... Садитесь!
issues.translation_quote: Uh... get in!
issues.justification: Minor; but 'Лэйтинант. Старшой я…' rendered 'Lieutenant. I'm a senior one...' loses the colloquial 'старшой'.
